Banner, C., Megaritis, A., Soler, A. and Yugo, M. (2019). Refinery 2050: Conceptual Assessment. Exploring opportunities and challenges for the EU refining industry to transition towards a low-CO2 intensive economy. Appendixes (report 9/19A, the appendixes of Concawe report no. 9/19). Concawe, Brussels, September 2019. Prepared for the Concawe Special Task Force Refinery 2050 (STF-2).

NO TECHNOLOGY DATA. 31-page appendix volume of Concawe 9/19; the technology modelling (hydrogen, electricity and processing requirements per low-carbon feedstock pathway, refinery configurations, CO2 results) is in the main report 9/19, which is not in the intake and should be requested. The appendixes hold: A1 a scope diagram; A2 a qualitative safety statement and air-quality literature review (A2-A3: percentage ranges of NOx, PM, VOC, CO changes for vegetable oils, algae, biomass gasification, waste plastics and e-fuels, no technology parameters); A4 a literature review of European and world biomass availability and demand 2020-2050 (Mtoe/a, mostly in bar charts without printed values; text figures: EU sustainable biomass about 175 Mtoe/a in 2020 to 350-535 Mtoe/a in 2050, EU Clean Planet strategy 210-320 Mtoe/a; advanced biofuel demand up to 70-140 Mtoe/a; e-fuels 0-71 Mtoe/a (EC), 80 Mtoe/a (DENA) in 2050), energy-content conversion factors (toe/t: agricultural residues 0.56, forestry 0.21, waste 0.76, algae 0.48; 1 toe = 41,868 GJ), and a TRL and cost overview taken from IRENA with charts only (Fig. A4-5 to A4-11). The only printed cost or capacity numbers: advanced biofuel capacity must rise from 0.2 GW to about 1.1 GW by 2020 at an estimated EUR 4.5-5 billion (30 GW in 2030, 250 GW in 2050 for the targets); advanced biofuel production costs expected 0.5-2 EUR/l diesel equivalent (below 2 EUR/l by 2050), aqueous phase reforming up to 2.4 EUR/l in 2030 falling to 1.9 EUR/l in 2050 (IRENA); competitive with fossil fuel above about 100 USD/bbl crude; biomass supply cost -2 to 8 EUR/GJ; feedstock 40-70% of production cost. All are sector-level or literature ranges without a technology, unit basis or price year, so nothing fits the per-technology archetype tables. Overlap with Concawe 8/19 (concawe_2019_001): none; 8/19 carries the refinery capex, opex and energy assumptions. If cited, use printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 2; roman front matter I-IV, body pages 4-28). Suggested source-id if registered later: concawe_2019_002.
